# pcd_compute_instance_lease (Resource)

Manages a VM's own lease in mors, PCD's VM lease service: a fixed time at which mors powers the VM off or deletes it, in place of the project's `pcd_compute_lease_policy`. This is the PCD UI's **Customize Lease** on a VM.

The VM's project must have a lease policy; create the policy in the same configuration and reference it through `project_id` so it is created first and destroyed last. `expiry` may be at most one policy period from the time of the apply, as in the PCD UI. Write it as a fixed time, or with the `hashicorp/time` provider's `time_offset`; `timeadd(timestamp(), ...)` changes on every plan.

~> mors checks leases about once a minute. Destroying this resource removes the VM's own lease, and the VM falls back to the project's policy, counted from its creation: a VM older than the policy is powered off or deleted within a minute. After a `power off` lease runs out, mors powers the VM off again on every pass: a `pcd_compute_instance` with `power_state = "active"` then starts it on every apply and mors stops it again, until the lease is extended. A `delete` lease deletes the VM, and its `pcd_compute_instance` then plans a new one. Deleting the project's policy also deletes this lease.

## Example Usage

```terraform
data "pcd_identity_project" "dev" {
  name = "dev"
}

resource "pcd_compute_lease_policy" "dev" {
  project_id     = data.pcd_identity_project.dev.id
  expiry_minutes = 3 * 24 * 60
}

data "pcd_networking_network" "dev" {
  name = "dev-network"
}

# The VM boots in the provider's project, here dev, the project of the policy.
resource "pcd_compute_instance" "build_agent" {
  name        = "build-agent"
  image_name  = "Ubuntu-22.04"
  flavor_name = "m1.small"

  network {
    uuid = data.pcd_networking_network.dev.id
  }
}

variable "build_agent_lease_renewal" {
  type        = number
  description = "Bump to move the build agent's lease two days past the apply."
  default     = 1
}

# Two days from the apply that created it (or last bumped the renewal), in the
# form mors takes. time_offset comes from the hashicorp/time provider; it keeps
# the value fixed between applies, where timeadd(timestamp(), ...) would change
# on every plan.
resource "time_offset" "build_agent_lease" {
  offset_days = 2
  triggers = {
    renewal = var.build_agent_lease_renewal
  }
}

# The build agent's own lease, in place of the project's three days. Setting
# project_id from the policy creates the policy first.
resource "pcd_compute_instance_lease" "build_agent" {
  instance_id = pcd_compute_instance.build_agent.id
  project_id  = pcd_compute_lease_policy.dev.project_id
  expiry      = time_offset.build_agent_lease.rfc3339
  action      = "power off"
}

# For a VM this configuration does not manage (created in the PCD UI, say),
# look it up by name with the pcd_compute_instance data source:
#
# data "pcd_compute_instance" "legacy" {
#   name = "legacy-build-agent"
# }
#
# resource "pcd_compute_instance_lease" "legacy" {
#   instance_id = data.pcd_compute_instance.legacy.id
#   project_id  = pcd_compute_lease_policy.dev.project_id
#   expiry      = time_offset.build_agent_lease.rfc3339
# }
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `expiry` (String) When the lease runs out, as a UTC time with whole seconds: `2026-12-31T23:59:59Z`. Must be in the future, and no later than one policy period from the time of the apply. Updated in place.
- `instance_id` (String) The VM the lease is for. For a VM this configuration does not manage, look it up with the `pcd_compute_instance` data source. Changing this forces a new resource.

### Optional

- `action` (String) What mors does when the lease runs out: `power off` (the default) or `delete`. Updated in place, which mors refuses once `expiry` has passed.
- `project_id` (String) The VM's project. Read from the VM when omitted; when set, it must be the VM's project, which the provider checks before writing the lease, because mors does not. Setting it to `pcd_compute_lease_policy.<name>.project_id` orders the lease after the policy. Changing this forces a new resource.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) `<project_id>/<instance_id>`.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax. The IDs are assigned by PCD; the
[Importing guide](https://registry.terraform.io/providers/platform9/pcd/latest/docs/guides/importing)
explains how to look them up.

```shell
# <project_id>/<instance_id>: pcdctl server show <name> -c project_id -c id
terraform import pcd_compute_instance_lease.build_agent <project_id>/<instance_id>
```
